articles.title: Raúl Varela: "Ya no se puede decir que trabajas menos que el que redacta comunicados en el Real Madrid"
articles.standfirst: El director de La Tribu critica la escalada entre Real Madrid y Atlético: "Aquí lo único que importa es ganar y saber aceptar con humildad cuando toca perder"
articles.summary: El director de La Tribu critica la escalada entre Real Madrid y Atlético: "Aquí lo único que importa es ganar y saber aceptar con humildad cuando toca perder"
articles.body: Raúl Varela puso el foco en La Tribu en la polémica que rodea al Real Madrid y al Atlético de Madrid después del derbi. El periodista cuestionó la escalada dialéctica entre los clubes y contrapuso ese ambiente con la imagen vivida en Las Rozas durante la jornada de puertas abiertas de la selección española. "Ya no se puede decir 'trabajas menos que el que redacta comunicados en el Real Madrid', o que el community manager del Atlético, que tanto monta, monta tanto. Ya han dejado de ser puestos soñados", comenzó Varela. El director de La Tribu considera que la situación empieza a sobrepasar los límites: "El caso empieza a dar un poco de cringe, que dice la juventud, ver enzarzarse a unos y otros haciéndose los dignos, porque la competición, nos explican, se mancilla con semejantes actitudes". Varela recordó diferentes polémicas que han acompañado al fútbol a lo largo de los años antes de lanzar un mensaje contundente: "Dejen ya de vacilarnos, de tratarnos como si necesitásemos una subvención". Para el periodista, detrás de toda la batalla posterior al derbi existe una cuestión mucho más sencilla: "Aquí lo único que importa es ganar y saber aceptar con humildad cuando toca perder, porque de esto va todo este rollo, de perder, en este caso el Madrid, pero ayer fue al contrario y mañana quizá también". Raúl Varela fue especialmente crítico con el clima generado alrededor de las polémicas: "Todo este ambiente putrefacto con una mercancía caducada que aún compran algunos en determinadas latitudes contrasta con la fiesta del fútbol que ayer volvió a vivirse en Las Rozas". La otra cara que destacó Varela fue la vivida alrededor de la selección española. Una jornada de puertas abiertas en Las Rozas en la que varios cientos de niños pudieron disfrutar de los internacionales. Varela puso como ejemplo la convivencia entre dos futbolistas que habían sido protagonistas directos del derbi: "Se entremezclan y se lo toman con mucha naturalidad Hjusen y Grimaldo, por citar a dos de los protagonistas de un derbi que empezó a resolverse precisamente por el penalti anotado por uno y cometido por el otro". El director de La Tribu defendió además el efecto de la selección sobre los futbolistas: "Ojalá haya más selecciones nacionales en el calendario de clubes, primero porque subliman el rendimiento y los títulos y segundo porque buena parte de ese éxito llega a través del buen comportamiento". Y cerró su opinión contraponiendo esa imagen con las disputas institucionales: "A tenor de lo visto ya empiezan a sobrar los bad boys de los despachos que no hacen más que mal meter en función de su conveniencia". Varela terminó con una petición cargada de ironía: "Pero como buen idealista que soy no pierdo la fe: un comunicado para comunicar que se acaban los comunicados".

articles.title: Barcelona face fresh wage bill warning despite staying within UEFA parameters
articles.summary: Barcelona have worked hard to regain financial stability, but a familiar concern is beginning to surface again: the cost of maintaining the first-team squad...
articles.body:
Barcelona have worked hard to regain financial stability, but a familiar concern is beginning to surface again: the cost of maintaining the first-team squad is rising.

According to AS , the club remains within the squad-cost parameters recommended by UEFA, and there is no immediate financial alarm.

However, the concern instead lies in the direction of travel, with Barcelona's wage bill increasing again after several years of efforts to bring spending under control.

Simply put, Barça have more room than they did during their recent financial struggles, but their spending cannot continue rising faster than their income indefinitely.

Barcelona's squad is becoming more expensive again

The increase in squad costs is partly a reflection of what has happened on the pitch.

Barcelona need to be very cautious about their spendings. (Photo by Eric Alonso/Getty Images)

Barcelona have enjoyed greater sporting success , while sporting director Deco has used the club's return to the 1:1 salary-cap rule to strengthen the squad and renew contracts.

That has allowed Barça to operate with considerably more freedom in the transfer market. The club made several significant additions during the summer while also committing more money to existing players.

At present, Barcelona remain within sustainable parameters and still have room for further growth. The important requirement, though, is that revenue continues to grow faster than expenditure.

Camp Nou and BLM hold the key to Barcelona's next step

Barcelona are counting heavily on increased commercial and matchday income to support the more expensive squad.

The renovated Spotify Camp Nou is expected to become a major source of revenue once fully operational, while Barça Licensing and Merchandising (BLM) is also expected to generate more money in the coming years.

Barcelona are currently operating under a safe zone. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

Those increases will be particularly significant because Barcelona are expected to return to the Lluis Companys stadium at the beginning of next season.

Playing there again will mean lower matchday revenues compared with the completed Camp Nou project.

AS therefore expects Barcelona to once again exceed their salary-cap limit next season, despite the club currently remaining within UEFA's recommended parameters.

Notably, that does not automatically point to another financial crisis, as the situation is more about maintaining the balance between an increasingly expensive squad and the income needed to support it.

articles.title: Liverpool wonderkid to be handed new role by Andoni Iraola amid contract talks
articles.summary: Rio Ngumoha is undoubtedly one of the most exciting talents in world football, but he has faced a tough start to the season. Despite being one of the brighte...
articles.body:
Rio Ngumoha is undoubtedly one of the most exciting talents in world football, but he has faced a tough start to the season.

Despite being one of the brightest parts of Liverpool 's dismal 2025/26 campaign, Ngumoha has struggled for minutes under Andoni Iraola and now finds himself behind £123 million signing Bradley Barcola in the pecking order.

Rio has played just 22% of the available minutes in the Premier League this season and is yet to register a goal or an assist in any competition.

The 18-year-old's talent is clear to see though, and Liverpool's priority remains continuing to develop their wonderkid into a superstar.

Rio Ngumoha 's Liverpool role going forward

Talks are reportedly underway to tie Ngumoha down to an extended contract on improved terms at Anfield in order to fend off interest from several of Europe's top clubs, including Arsenal .

Progress on a new deal has been slow however, leading some to suggest that the teenager's lack of minutes this season could be a roadblock in negotiations.

According to a new report from Football Insider , the youngster is content with his situation at Anfield and will not push for a move away any time soon, with the promise of a regular starting role in place.

Rio could earn his second cap for England this international break, and a good performance on the international stage could accelerate negotiations over a fresh deal.

The winger's current deal isn't set to expire until 2028, but the 20-time Premier League champions are keen to tie him down to a longer deal to make sure his future lies in Merseyside.

With a lack of depth on the wings, minutes will keep coming Rio's way and it is likely only a matter of time until the Englishman finds the back of the net again for the Reds.

articles.title: Nations League: The rise of Liverpool and Wales' Lewis Koumas
articles.summary: Having made his mark in the early stages of the season at Liverpool, Lewis Koumas will aim to continue his good form with Wales in the Nations League.
articles.body:
By the looks of it, Lewis Koumas is not wasting his time.

It took less than a week of pre-season for the 21-year-old to show new Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola what he could offer.

And it has taken less than a month of the new season for him to show why he has a place in Liverpool's plans.

Now, over the next fortnight, the attacking prospect who is fast becoming an Anfield favourite will attempt to prove what several people in Welsh football have suspected for a long while - that he can have a big impact on the international stage too.

"I feel he's going to be a really important player for us for a number of years," Wales boss Craig Bellamy said before Nations League games with Portugal, Denmark and Norway that will see Koumas share an international stage with the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo and Erling Haaland.

Live on BBC iPlayer, BBC One Wales, BBC Sounds, BBC Radio Wales, Radio Cymru and 5 Live, BBC Sport website and app, plus live text commentary.

Bellamy is not alone. Wales and Liverpool legend Ian Rush is among a growing number impressed by Koumas' potential, a potential that – despite his recent rise to prominence – has been obvious for a number of years.

Right from the off, in fact. The surname alone brought excitement, given the talents of Lewis' father, former Wales international Jason Koumas.

"Jason was a talented, talented player," says Danny Gabbidon, who played alongside the older Koumas for Wales.

"He could do a bit of everything; technically amazing, he could look after the ball, pass, score fantastic goals. He could just make things happen."

The phrase mercurial midfielder never felt more fitting than for Koumas senior, who won 34 caps and scored 10 goals for Wales but could delight and frustrate in equal measure.

"He could be a bit lazy at times," chuckles Gabbidon when considering a player who was often nonchalance personified.

Indeed, Tranmere Rovers, West Bromwich Albion, Cardiff City and Wigan Athletic fans will all smile at the highlight-reel memories, while having a nagging feeling of what might have been had Koumas had the tenacity to match his talent.

Yet it seems Lewis has some of the qualities his father may have lacked.

"You wouldn't have seen Jason running around like Lewis the other night [for Liverpool against Tottenham] ," says Gabbidon.

"I kept a close eye on him because I've felt his best position is a striker and I've been keen to see him down the middle.

"To get the chance at a club like Liverpool shows what the manager thinks of him. But it's not just his talent, it's the appetite."

Name Wales' Euro 2016 semi-final XI against Ronaldo's Portugal

The younger Koumas' attitude is something that has been noted for some time.

Former Liverpool Under-21 head coach Barry Lewtas describes him as "a coach's dream".

"The effort, the will to learn and develop, how he applies himself, it's all there," Lewtas says.

A Liverpool supporter from birth, Koumas has been with the Reds since primary school age, following in the footsteps of his father, who was once a nine-year-old team-mate of Steven Gerrard and Michael Owen.

While Jason moved on to Tranmere without making the breakthrough at Liverpool, Lewis has flourished with the Premier League giants, especially since being pushed from midfield into a forward role at the age of 16.

"That was an important part of his development, getting that exposure of playing deeper, dealing with the ball and the technical side," adds Lewtas.

"But then, when your skill-sets develop, you find the area that suits you best."

Given the influence of then Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp, Lewtas says Koumas' finishing prowess combined with a ferocious attitude towards pressing meant his path was obvious.

"He fitted us and we fitted him," Lewtas says.

By 2024, Klopp had given Koumas his senior debut.

He scored in the FA Cup against Southampton in February 2024 was then an unused substitute as Liverpool beat Chelsea to win the League Cup at Wembley.

There were more than 900 days before his next first-team appearance for Liverpool, with three loan spells in the Championship in between.

At Stoke City, Koumas played under three different managers in a single season, but earned roles under all three during a spell credited for boosting his belief.

He played 25 times for Birmingham City in the first half last season - though managed only seven league starts - before moving on to Hull City and playing an important role in the Tigers' promotion via the play-offs.

Koumas returned to Liverpool in the summer with renewed confidence.

The assumption was that another loan spell beckoned, but Iraola put a stop to such thoughts a week into the club's pre-season trip to the United States.

A Premier League debut followed, as did a first appearance in the Champions League, plus a relentless man-of-the-match performance against Tottenham that enamoured him to the Anfield crowd and seemed to symbolise the demands of the club's new boss.

Wales will have no fear in Portugal - James

Wilson, Darlow and Broadhead out of Wales squad

How to follow Wales in the Nations League on the BBC

"He's really matured since making his debut," says Theo Squires, senior football writer at the Liverpool Echo.

"Back then he was just a boy who had caught the eye at academy level as a versatile forward with a keen eye for goal.

"He looks almost unrecognisable physically. Leading the line against Tottenham, he more than held his own and he was a constant nuisance with his pace and never-say-die pressing."

Koumas' energy was described by Iraola as being contagious for the rest of the Liverpool squad, £100m-plus signings included.

"It's been brilliant to see," adds Lewtas. "But it's not just a case of running about and working hard, it's his intelligence. He doesn't just understand what to do, but why he's doing it."

Koumas knows what he is capable of, too.

Matty Jones, the Wales Under-21 head coach, has spoken of the regular meetings he had with Koumas to ensure there was no chance of England nabbing the Wirral-born Welshman.

One ended with Koumas telling Jones: "I'll win you games".

A match-winning, curling finish on his international under-21 debut in 2025 backed up the quiet self-assurance.

Before last June's senior international friendlies, Koumas said Wales fans had not seen "anything from me yet".

He pointed that having played only cameo roles for Wales, he needed to "work harder and show a little bit more to get the trust of the gaffer".

He duly scored his first international goal against Ghana.

"He's been there in every squad I've announced but I felt in the summer, he turned," says Bellamy. "When he came on against Ghana, he changed it completely – and he's a player who's capable of that.

"He's just coming into his own now and kicking on again – and to be the top player we expect him to be, that has to be the case."

Both club and international bosses agree there is more to work on, but also that there is more to come.

Wales will hope that he can make further strides during a demanding Nations League campaign which begins against Portugal in Lisbon on Thursday.

"He knows there is a higher ceiling," says Lewtas.

"Knowing Lewis' appetite for things, he won't be worried about it, he'll be looking forward to it."

articles.title: Tebas replies to Real Madrid’s statement asking for him to step down as La Liga president
articles.summary: La Liga president Javier Tebas posted a reply to Real Madrid’s statement asking for him to step down as La Liga president following his comments about the co...
articles.body:
La Liga president Javier Tebas posted a reply to Real Madrid 's statement asking for him to step down as La Liga president following his comments about the controversy during Sunday's Madrid Derbi against Atlético de Madrid .

I have read the statement. I fully agree with one sentence: the president of LaLiga is not the owner of the competition. Neither is the president of Real Madrid.

Representing all clubs requires defending equality and fairness among them. Also when it is stated that "LaLiga is worth nothing" without Real Madrid or that the referees harm "the business that feeds them." On those assertions, which motivated my response, your statement says not a word.

Now they hide behind the fact that I responded to an "independent" journalist. But neither the narrative is new, nor is the strategy of diverting attention from other problems. They have been doing it for years from Real Madrid TV and through their spokespeople, talking and writing about a rigged League week after week. Don't pretend to present as an outside opinion the discourse they fuel from their own television and from within the club.

They demand that I contribute to generating confidence in the impartiality of the competition. Precisely for that reason, I reject the narrative that referees are directed against Real Madrid. Criticizing a referee's decision is legitimate. Turning every perceived harm into proof of a persecution is another thing. Does that generate confidence or does it damage the image of Spanish football?

They confuse neutrality with independence. If by neutrality they mean not taking sides on anything, not even between what is right and what is wrong, they are asking me to renounce my responsibility. Independence requires deciding with one's own judgment, without pressures or subordination, applying the same rules to everyone and defending the common interest. That implies making decisions and taking a stand, even if Real Madrid doesn't like it.

Defending the interests of a club does not mean adopting its discourse. And representing everyone does not mean obeying the most powerful. The interests of the competition, of LaLiga, must be defended.

I am not the owner of LaLiga, nor will I manage it as if it belonged to a single club. I respect everyone. Subordination to no one. Source: Tebas' X account

articles.title: Barcelona legend Sergio Busquets takes first major step towards coaching career
articles.summary: Sergio Busquets has begun the next chapter of his football career.At 38, the former Barcelona midfielder is taking his first official steps towards becoming...
articles.body:
Sergio Busquets has begun the next chapter of his football career.

At 38, the former Barcelona midfielder is taking his first official steps towards becoming a coach, working as an assistant to Juliano Belletti with Barça Atlètic while preparing to begin his coaching qualifications in the coming weeks.

Busquets is still a familiar presence around the club, but his role has changed dramatically, as the player who spent years controlling matches on the pitch is now learning how to influence them from the technical area.

Busquets starts learning the coaching trade at Barça Atlètic

Notably, Busquets joined Belletti's Barça Atlètic staff in August after Barcelona announced his appointment as an assistant coach.

According to Mundo Deportivo , though, his involvement has so far been deliberately understated.

Busquets has joined Juliano Belletti at Barça Atlètic. (Photo courtesy: FC Barcelona official website)

Rather than taking an interventionist role, the former midfielder has spent much of his time observing training and matches, with his communication with players limited to occasional tactical comments.

His conversations have been particularly focused on midfielders, an area he knows better than almost anyone after building an extraordinary playing career in that position.

For now, his work is largely taking place away from the spotlight. He attends training sessions and matches at the Johan Cruyff Stadium, although he has not yet travelled with the team and currently watches matches from the stands.

Barcelona legend prepares for UEFA coaching licence

According to the outlet, Busquets is due to begin the UEFA A coaching course in the coming weeks. Until the course starts, he cannot officially take his place on the touchline during matches.

Once enrolled, he will receive provisional registration that will allow him to work from the technical area.

Busquets will soon begin the official work to get his coaching licence. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

Notably, his decision to join Barça Atlètic before beginning the course is intended to give him an early understanding of the job and ensure he enters the qualification process better prepared.

The UEFA A licence will allow him to coach at certain levels, including the Juvenil A category, or work as an assistant coach with a first team.

The eventual target is the UEFA PRO licence, which is the highest coaching qualification and is required to manage teams at the top level.

Those close to the Barcelona legend say his interest in coaching developed during the final years of his playing career.

After retiring in December at 37, he has now chosen to begin that transition at the club where he built his legacy.

articles.title: Stephen A. Smith believes 'special' Ole Miss QB Trinidad Chambliss is Heisman leader
articles.summary: Trinidad Chambliss reached the Division II mountaintop with Ferris State, worked hard to secure the starting job at Ole Miss and led the Rebels to a program-...
articles.body:
Trinidad Chambliss reached the Division II mountaintop with Ferris State, worked hard to secure the starting job at Ole Miss and led the Rebels to a program-redefining victory over Georgia in the Sugar Bowl. Now, after securing an injunction to play one final season, the 24-year-old quarterback has a chance to win the Heisman Trophy , capture an FBS title and complete one of the most incredible college football careers of all-time.

He has a long way to go, but Stephen A. Smith loves what this fierce competitor has accomplished through three games of the 2026 campaign. The prominent ESPN personality believes Chambliss is presently the most deserving man to bring home one of the most prestigious awards in sports.

"If Trinidad's last name was Manning , would he not be the {Heisman} favorite?" he said on SiriusXM's "The Stephen A. Smith Show." " Arch Manning can play. I like him a lot, but Trinidad Chambliss, at least on this level, the brother's special. Everybody better step up and recognize this. It's very, very important that you all know it. I mean it when I say it to you. I have him as the leading candidate for the Heisman."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Although much can change between now and the Heisman Trophy Ceremony, Chambliss has indeed been among the most impressive signal-callers in the country to this point. He helped his team survive Louisville at a neutral site in Ole Miss' season opener and overshadowed Lane Kiffin's return to Oxford by dissecting LSU's defense. This player has the stats and results that voters crave.

Arch Manning can build a case if Texas stays No. 1 and Mississippi State's Kamario Taylor is captivating fans around the nation, but Chambliss appears to be the leading SEC QB in the Heisman race at this time. Darian Mensah and Jayden Maiava are strong contenders in their own right, though, not to mention 2025 finalist Julian Sayin and Josh Hoover. Jeremiah Smith and Malachi Toney are talented enough to make wide receiver history, so this could be a crowded field.

Trinidad Chambliss is positioned to become the clear man in front, however. If he can lead the Rebels to a win versus No. 21 Florida in The Swamp, he will have prevailed against three ranked opponents in the first month of the season. There will be plenty of time to discuss No. 6's size and NFL potential , but Stephen A. Smith is right to extol his college excellence.

This repeatedly underestimated athlete is making magic with Ole Miss football , and if Chambliss continues to wave the magic wand, then he may have to prepare a big speech in December.

articles.title: Real Madrid decide 19-year-old first-team midfielder will play for Castilla after lengthy knee injury
articles.summary: Real Madrid have decided to give Thiago Pitarch his first competitive minutes of the season with Castilla as the midfielder continues his recovery from a kne...
articles.body:
Real Madrid have decided to give Thiago Pitarch his first competitive minutes of the season with Castilla as the midfielder continues his recovery from a knee injury.

According to Mundo Deportivo , the move has been agreed in advance between the club and the 19-year-old and is designed to give him the match exposure he needs after missing Jose Mourinho's entire pre-season and the start of the 2026/27 season.

Notably, Pitarch remains part of Mourinho's first-team setup despite being officially registered with Castilla.

Hence, the plan is for him to use the international break to rebuild his match fitness before returning to the senior squad once the window closes.

Pitarch set for Castilla return against Sant Andreu

The midfielder is expected to feature for Castilla against Sant Andreu at Can Drago on Wednesday, in a fixture that was postponed last weekend because of the Under-20 Intercontinental Cup.

Thiago Pitarch is yet to play under Jose Mourinho. (Photo by Charlotte Tattersall/Getty Images)

For Pitarch, the game would be an important step after months of rehabilitation . His recovery has followed the timeline established by Real Madrid, and the club now believes competitive football is the right way to test his knee.

The decision has been taken collectively by Real Madrid, Mourinho and the player, with the priority being to avoid rushing him directly back into first-team football.

Pitarch has already been involved with Mourinho's senior squad on several occasions but has yet to make his competitive debut.

Castilla therefore provides a controlled environment in which he can gradually build his rhythm.

Real Madrid could give Pitarch more minutes

For what it is worth, the Castilla assignment may not be limited to one appearance, as Pitarch has a serious chance of featuring against Alcorcon on September 27 and Atletico Madrid B on October 2.

Thiago Pitarch will play for Castilla during the international break. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

Both Primera RFEF fixtures will take place at the Alfredo Di Stefano Stadium, giving Pitarch further opportunities to increase his workload without immediately being exposed to the demands of first-team football.

That could be particularly useful given the midfielder missed the entire pre-season with Mourinho's squad.

As such, competitive minutes will allow Real Madrid to assess how his knee responds before he returns to the senior group.

The expectation, after the aforementioned, is that Pitarch will rejoin the first team after the international break.

His Castilla spell should therefore be viewed as part of the final stage of his recovery rather than a change in his position within Mourinho's plans.

articles.standfirst: El jugador llegó los últimos días de mercado, sin haber hecho una pretemporada en condiciones en Liverpool y llegó excedido de peso: tiene tres semanas para ponerse a punto
articles.summary: El jugador llegó los últimos días de mercado, sin haber hecho una pretemporada en condiciones en Liverpool y llegó excedido de peso: tiene tres semanas para ponerse a punto
articles.body: Harvey Elliott, por lo visto en los pocos minutos de los que ha dispuesto desde que ha llegado al Valencia en calidad de cedido por el Liverpool, es un 'quiero pero no puedo'. Su condición física tiene que ser óptima para poder desarrollar sus virtudes en plenitud y de momento no ha sido así porque el jugador británico llegó fuera de forma. Hasta cierto punto lógico, puesto que no contaba para los 'Reds' y le buscaban salida. Hizo una pretemporada atípica. Y es ahora cuando lo está pagando. Se ha visto en los partidos que ha jugado con el Valencia. Ante el Barcelona (36 minutos), el Sevilla (28') y la Real Sociedad (21') -contra el Alavés ni siquiera tuvo minutos por la exigencia del guion de partido-. Dista mucho de ser el Elliott del pasado que deslumbraba con la calidad que tiene en sus botas. Y no luce porque está fuera de forma. Llegó lejos de los limites del peso óptimo para su físico. Y es ahora cuando debe ponerse en forma. Esta es una 'pretemporada' casi hecha para él. De los que más debería aprovechar un calendario como el que hay donde no hay fútbol durante tres semanas. Para Elliott jugar en el Valencia es una prueba exigente. Porque debe recuperar un punto de juego que le hizo brillara para ser uno de los 'niños de oro' de la Inglaterra del futuro. Pero los últimos dos años esa perspectiva tan positiva se había detenido en el tiempo. El futbolista necesita un cambio de aires radical y la Liga y el Valencia eran una buena salida para desintoxicarse. Pero de momento está pagando no estar en forma y es ahora cuando debe poner todo de su parte para que en estas tres semanas llegue al punto ideal con el que poder sumar. Cabe recordar que la cesión de Harvey Elliott -por un año sin opción a nada más- ha supuesto un gran desembolso para el Valencia. Porque paga casi íntegra una 'ficha Premier' que para como está el Valencia ya supone mucho. Aun así, y sin pagar la totalidad de la misma, se trata del tercer jugador con el contrato más alto de la actual plantilla y se le debe exigir como tal. De momento, Elliott se busca. Necesita encontrar su peso ideal para poder ser Harvey Elliott.

articles.title: Roberto Mancini returns as Italy head coach but can the Azzurri recover from lowest ebb with a youth-inspired revolution?
articles.summary: Roberto Mancini is back as Italy head coach after a second spell; the former Man City boss won Euro 2020 with the Azzurri, who have not qualified for the last three World Cups; With exclusive insight from Gianluigi Donnarumma, Sky Sports' Sam Blitz analyses the road back for Italy...
articles.body:
Italy did not qualify for the third World Cup in a row. An unthinkable prospect given they have won the competition four times.

The first two failures to qualify were masked over by the Euro 2020 triumph at Wembley. That at least gave the nation hope.

The third World Cup failure was one last straw. A 48-team World Cup did not include Italy. It brought about the resignations of not just head coach Gennaro Gattuso, but also Italian FA president Gabriele Gravina and Gianluigi Buffon as the team's head of delegation.

"It's a sensitive subject that affects me a lot, because not qualifying for three World Cups in a row is tough, and Italy certainly doesn't deserve that," Italy captain Gianluigi Donnarumma tells Sky Sports .

Now Italy have gone back to the future. Roberto Mancini, the manager who won the Euros five years ago, is back at the helm.

"We have to work. The only way forward is to work," adds Donnarumma. "There has now been a change of coach, the return of Mr Mancini - and the objective is to work and try to take Italy back to where it deserves to be.

"I know it's not easy for the fans, but especially for us, because only we know how much it means to us to play in a competition like the World Cup.

"So we'll give everything to bring Italy back to where it deserves to be. We have a great responsibility because history says that Italy should always be there. History has taught us that. So we have to bring Italy back to where it belongs."

Yes, Italy belongs at the top table. But it has been far off the level for some time. The latest World Cup disaster was the latest in a long line of slippery slopes since they reached the top of the world in 2006.

Twenty years later, that penalty shoot-out win over France is still Italy's last appearance in a World Cup knockout game. They have just won just one World Cup match since then - the 2-1 victory over England in Brazil 2014.

Yes, there was the successful European Championships campaign of 2012 that saw Italy reach the final. But since those days, Italy have not been the same. And there are multiple reasons for it.

Italy have not been able to replicate the world-class talent they once possessed. The World Cup-winning side of 20 years ago had the likes of Fabio Cannavaro, Alessandro Nesta, Gattuso and Alessandro Del Piero.

Six years later in 2012, that generation still lived on through Buffon, Daniele De Rossi, and Andrea Pirlo. But since the retirement of stalwarts Giorgio Chiellini and Leandro Bonucci, the next generation of Italian football has been lost.

According to the CIES Football Observatory, between 2020 and 2025, Italy produced just 413 football exports. It ranked 24th in the world, behind the United States, Japan and Russia.

The other four nations in Europe's big five leagues all managed over 1,000 players in the same category. Italy's players - young or old - are just not as fancied by Europe's elite.

The lack of quality coming from the Italian ranks could also be seen in the national team. Between June 2025 and February 2026, only one capped player for the national team was under the age of 24 - Inter's young forward Pio Esposito. England managed a dozen in the same period.

In 2025, Italy also gave 1.9 per cent of their Serie A minutes to eligible players under the age of 21. That was the second-lowest out of the top 50 leagues in world football. Only the United Arab Emirates Pro League managed fewer.

It also contributed to a weaker Serie A last season. Veteran players Kevin De Bruyne, Luka Modric and Jamie Vardy were among the high-profile signings. And there was a similar lack of creativity amongst the managers too.

The likes of Antonio Conte, Max Allegri, Gattuso, Luciano Spalletti and Maurizio Sarri have all been passed around the top Italian clubs without much variation. Even this summer, Sarri moved to Atalanta, while Allegri joined Juventus.

Cesc Fabregas' Como revolution - resulting in their Champions League qualification earlier this year - is exactly what can happen when tactical ideas emerge from outside that never-ending cycle. Ruben Amorim has also turned up at AC Milan and played some eye-catching football with the Rossoneri.

But there are some signs that times could be changing for Italy. Mancini's first Italy squad back contained a few positive surprises. A 34-player roster included nine uncapped players - and 11 players under the age of 23.

That includes Borussia Dortmund's 18-year-old striker Samuele Inacio, Chelsea-bound defender Honest Ahanor, now at Crystal Palace. Brentford's Michael Kayode is among the new 'young revolution'.

As well as Inacio and highly-rated Inter forward Esposito - who has five goals in nine Italy caps - there is also FC Nurnberg's Ali Zoma who has 20 goals in 36 appearances in the German second division. Midfielder Issa Doumbia is also a key player at Sporting CP this season.

There's a new generation of young Italian stars.

"There will certainly be some established players. We're getting older, but we're still young, and there will also be some very young players joining the team," says Donnarumma.

"So it will be a mixture, and we need to help these young players integrate well. They can give us a great deal of help.

"They're certainly talented players who need to play and gain experience, but I'm sure Italy will return to where it belongs."

Italy have a very tricky Nations League group, with Belgium, Turkey and France competing in a very competitive Group A.

But a nation who has been lingering in the dark for so long needs just one spark.
